extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed for college-level multi-discipline multimodal understanding and reasoning, featuring 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks spanning six core disciplines.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Over 50 university students were recruited to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions sourced from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, online sources, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning involved identifying potential duplicates using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, followed by manual review to eliminate duplications. Problems were checked for format and typos, categorized into four difficulty levels, and approximately 10% of the problems classified as very easy were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. They were advised to select questions without immediately available answers to prevent data contamination.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Suspected duplicates were reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format, undertaking necessary corrections where deviations were found.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: A team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to monitor progress towards Expert AGI, which could reach the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor, leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and the 90th percentile of skilled adults, and college exams are not the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. The manual curation process may also carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluating multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning, specifically under a zero-shot setting.

name.evidence: We introduce MMMU : a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning.

description.evidence: MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: In the second stage, we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: drawing from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking... In the third and final stage, the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels... Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: The annotators are instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Given the arising data contamination concems of foundation models, the annotators are advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking. This step requires authors to ensure adherence to a standardized format, undertaking necessary corrections where deviations are found.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: The questions in our benchmark were manually collected by a team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: It denotes an AI system that reaches “at least 90th percentile of skilled adults” in a broad range of tasks, thus starting to achieve “the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor” for many industries, leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. Therefore, it is of both intellectual and societal importance to closely monitor the progress towards Expert AGI.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI [57].

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We shall caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as per the definition [57], because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and “90th percentile of skilled adults,” nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. ... The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI [57].

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We introduce MMMU : a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. ... Our evaluation is conducted under a zero-shot setting to assess the capability of models to generate accurate answers without fine-tuning or few-shot demonstrations on our benchmark.
